- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/fan-out-system-context.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **20** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93e6c1a5f8bf256310f9ed477523ff2c90bf1bff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fe42e502a67d65872a9c0130a3c4e586401f7ac6` — the merge of head `1408bfb197cf80b2d3dea541d14c9b9f2efdbe65` into base `93e6c1a5f8bf256310f9ed477523ff2c90bf1bff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fe42e502a67d65872a9c0130a3c4e586401f7ac6 && git checkout fe42e502a67d65872a9c0130a3c4e586401f7ac6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93e6c1a5f8bf256310f9ed477523ff2c90bf1bff 1408bfb197cf80b2d3dea541d14c9b9f2efdbe65 && git checkout -B drift-repro 93e6c1a5f8bf256310f9ed477523ff2c90bf1bff && git merge --no-ff 1408bfb197cf80b2d3dea541d14c9b9f2efdbe65

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93e6c1a5f8bf256310f9ed477523ff2c90bf1bff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 93e6c1a5f8bf256310f9ed477523ff2c90bf1bff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 · 2026-10-21T00:58Z

`os-justin` · `session_011TdZ8GjixNZFLz1xJD9zzK` (seat post #6021). Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main` `62bc129308`, not against the report (os-dev report `6305012957` on #24978).

Head under review:

```text
1408bfb197cf80b2d3dea541d14c9b9f2efdbe65
```

1. **Shape.**
   - Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #24978`. Line-start `Clause-②: yes (widening)` appears in the body and in the `service-messaging` changeset.
   - 19 files, +1821/−94, none on a governed surface (`governedPathsIn` answers `[]`). The trial merge onto `origin/main` is clean.
   - The review face is `declaration` at `TIER_DEFAULT` (no schema, no governed path, no narrowing declared), so this ACCEPT is the review of record of the widening, read below sentence by sentence.
   - `packages/spec` is untouched. PR #24940's 34 `plugin-approvals` test files are untouched; the new pins are new files.
2. **The contract, read in the code against the PR body's five sentences.**
   - **① Widened.** `EmitInput.keyedText?` is optional and additive. Every input accepted before is still accepted. True in `messaging-service.ts`: the member is read only when present.
   - **② Closed shape, refused at emit.** `assertNotificationTextKeys` runs first in `emit()`, before the dedup read and before any write. It refuses an undeclared member, a key with no face, a param name no hole can spell, a keyed param without `fallback`, and the absence of both keys. It narrows nothing that existed. A key that could never render is a loud error, not a literal delivered forever, which is the frame's AI-authoring axis.
   - **③ Delivered text.**
     - One `NotificationTextRenderer` is composed by `MessagingServicePlugin` and handed to both the service (inline `fanOut`, rendered once per recipient for all of their channels) and the dispatcher (`processRow`, and each row of a digest group). So one recipient gets one language on every channel.
     - The language is `resolveRecipientLocale` (#13881), negotiated by `resolveBundleLocale`.
     - Each member falls back to the literal.
     - Without `keyedText`, `fanOut` hands every channel the very object it did before, and no locale is read.
   - **④ The snapshot reserves `keyedText`.** Read as part of the widening; the open question is ruled below.
   - **⑤ Unchanged.** The event row, recipients, preferences, availability and the `template` path. A literal-only emit is pinned byte-unchanged against a service with no renderer.
3. **The catalog.**
   - It is the `i18n` service's existing catalog, in the declared `messages` face, the shape `plugin-audit`'s `messages.mentionedYou` already uses. ⛔ There is no second catalog.
   - The Operation Message Catalog (`errors.ID`, refusals) was measured and correctly not reused.
   - Read against the spec's retired object-first `notifications` key (`translation.zod.ts:605`, "notifications have no translation group"): that guidance retires a top-level authoring group, and this PR adds no such group and no spec key. Producer sentences live in the producer's `messages` face.
4. **The emitters.**
   - All 14 `notify()` sites in `approval-service.ts` pass keys. The `en` entries interpolated are byte-identical to the previous literals (pinned).
   - The subject keeps ruling B's "object label + id" form, with the label as a keyed param (`objects.<object>.label`, falling back to the schema label).
   - A person's own words (a comment, a request for information, a send-back note) stay as written; only their headlines are keyed.
   - Five sibling notifications beyond the card's named six are converted under the bounded in-place rule. They are named in the body, all four conditions hold, and the seat accepts them.
5. **Pins and ablation.**
   - `service-messaging`: `keyed-notification-text.integration.test.ts`, 10 cases. They cover the inline, durable and digest paths, a zh-CN recipient, bare `zh`, the deployment default, a miss falling back, a literal-only emit unchanged, the reserved snapshot name, and refusal at emit.
   - `plugin-approvals`: `approval-notification-keyed-text.integration.test.ts`, 5 cases. They cover every topic carrying its key, locale parity, and end to end with a real `MessagingService` and inbox.
   - Ablation: 10 legs, each red on its pin. Every restore was proven by blob equality and an empty `git diff HEAD`.
6. **Changesets.** `@objectstack/service-messaging` `minor` (rule 「甲」: an 18.x minor) and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` `patch` (no accept set or export of the plugin moves). Each was read sentence by sentence, and each matches 2–4.
7. **The open question, ruled by the seat: A, keep the reservation as shipped.**
   - **Real need:** no producer writes `payload.keyedText` (measured: 0 hits outside the two packages).
   - **Long-term:** the snapshot keeps one owner for its reserved names, the rule it already applies to `title`, `body`, `severity`, `actionUrl` and `actorId`.
   - **AI authoring:** the axis splits. C (refusal at emit) is the louder answer, while A drops a same-named producer member silently. A still makes keyed rendering reachable only through the typed, validated member, and it spends no accept-set narrowing on a name nobody writes.
   - **Startup scope:** A adds no surface and no gate.
   - The maintainer may veto toward C. That would be a separate narrowing card, and nothing in this PR forecloses it.
8. **Gates.**
   - At ACCEPT, every check-run on this head is `success` or an expected skip. Among them are TypeScript Type Check, the Lint lanes, Test Core 1–6/6, Build Core, Validate Package Dependencies, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Check Documentation Links.
   - Locally, all 84 derived families exited 0, and `--ran` reads 0 NOT MEASURED.
   - `service-messaging`: 618 tests passed. `plugin-approvals`: 1208 tests passed.
9. **Accepted deviations.**
   - One merge of `main`.
   - The lockfile carries only the 3-line `plugin-approvals` importer entry, where `pnpm install` had reshuffled two unrelated peers. Those hunks were discarded, and `--frozen-lockfile` exits 0.
   - A `service-messaging` devDependency and an anchored source alias in `plugin-approvals`' `vitest.config.ts` (`check:test-source-alias` green).
   - WIP commit subjects, which the squash replaces.
   - A long hold of the verify lock, flagged by the lock itself.
   - Model-free trailers.
10. **Out-of-scope disposition.**
   - The digest heading is an English literal for every recipient. It is filed as #25015, for triage.
   - `plugin-audit`'s `collab.mention` title: the dev noted it as carrier none. The seat read `audit-writers.ts:2506`. It is emitted once per mentioned user and already rendered in that user's locale, at emit, through the ADR-0053 write-locale chain. Whether that chain can answer differently from #13881's is unmeasured, so no defect has reach and no card is filed (filing gate ①).
11. **Landing clause.** Tier S: not governed, under the human-merge threshold. Next step: ready + auto-merge through the relay once every check on the current head is green or an expected skip. A push resets this reading.
